# R377 — supplemental phase hash and slot diagnostic consumers

Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo). Read-only source/spec audit. Target worktree W is `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013`, supplied clean HEAD `0f1127823e6c77f324093d9ffcf42cb773ce8ced`. Its lifetime summary pins relevant phase sources to the prior source parent `54385d6f975a13df5da87f489614d0b729d2aba6`; current `expert_cache.cpp` hash in that pin is `e50a8a77402108a092eeb5e404c9b47cef2ee617dd44fbbacec093172696735c`. Latest registry v188 declares exactly 917 completed research reports. Required prior context: R360, R362, R367, R375, and `bench/results/2026-10-13-phase-cache-model-lifetime/summary.json`.

No build, test, import/AST, GPU/model, profiler, service/process, Git, or cleanup action was performed. No active Main measurement artifact was read. Only this report is written.

## Finding

The current per-slot FNV-1a64 pass and `slot_checked` stderr line are supplemental diagnostics after a successful `PhaseCacheOwner::fill_checked`. They are not part of the slot admission, staged publication, reader-ready state, or return-value contract. The current exact payload gate is the full source-to-readback `memcmp`, reached only after a successful write and successful read whose SYCL operation completion is checked by the backend path. `fill_checked` marks `filled_` and `staged_` only after that equality passes. `phase_publish` separately checks the complete host/device residency table before `PhaseCacheOwner::publish` exposes the staged table. A mismatch or transfer error retains the existing fail-stop behavior.

Accordingly, source design can make the FNV traversal and verbose per-slot line optional for a quiet performance mode while keeping exact equality, checked completion, staged publication and fail-stop handling unconditional. The safe switch controls only whether the extra source-byte fingerprint is computed and whether its line is emitted. Do not gate the readback, compare, completion checks, source lifetime, or any owner state change. Keep the detailed mode available for diagnostics. No implementation or runtime behavior was changed or qualified here.

## Source consumer and contract audit

`src/core/expert_cache.cpp:198-210` calls `phase_->fill_checked(...)`; failure immediately returns false. Only on success does it increment bounded `fills_`, calculate the local FNV-1a64 value, print `strata phase-cache: slot_checked layer=... expert=... slot=... bytes=... fnv1a64=...`, and return true. The routine's caller contract in `include/strata/core/expert_cache.hpp` returns a boolean/error and does not expose or consume the hash.

`src/core/phase_cache_owner.cpp:282-311` sets `readers_ready_ = false`, validates source geometry and ownership admission, calls backend write, then backend read into `verification_`, times and checks `memcmp(source, verification_, bytes)`, and only then records `filled_` and `staged_`. The hash runs after this method returns. This separates the hash from the exact payload correctness condition. `PhaseCacheOwner::publish` is another boundary: it checks the staged table through the upload callback and only commits it to `published_`/reader-visible state after callback success. These contracts are the invariants a diagnostic switch must preserve.

In the inspected code tree, the only `phase_fill` call sites are the initial 144 baseline fills and successful-prompt extra fills in `src/program/generate.cpp` (around lines 4553 and 8037). The only `slot_checked`/`fnv1a64=` string consumer found under `src/`, `include/`, `tests/`, and `tools/` is the emitting `fprintf`; no production logic, test assertion, or controller implementation in those source trees parses it. `src/core/pinned.cpp` and `src/core/expert_source.cpp` use the general `fnv1a64` helper for unrelated arena/source fingerprints, so changing or bypassing this local `phase_fill` loop must not alter those other hash contracts. This search does not establish whether an external or closed-run measurement controller parses `slot_checked`; inspect a controller only after its run is closed before removing the line from any diagnostic protocol.

The line provides one human-readable record per successfully checked slot, including selected layer/expert/slot/byte count and a source hash. That is useful when diagnosing which source-to-slot transfer was attempted and comparing source identity across separately recorded runs. It is not independent evidence of destination bytes because the hash is of `source`, not readback/destination, and it is emitted only after the exact comparison succeeded. The exact comparison is stronger for the current copy-time correctness question. A compact always-on aggregate (`calls`, bytes, failures, checked completion and mismatch count) may retain run accounting without printing 768 lines; if per-slot mapping evidence is needed, keep an explicit diagnostic mode or a bounded structured summary.

## Candidate choices and limits

1. **Diagnostic gate (smallest and lowest semantic risk):** a quiet-mode option disables only the source FNV loop and per-slot formatting/write. Resolve it once per cache/run, not by repeated environment parsing per slot. Defaulting detailed diagnostics on preserves current diagnostic expectations; the quiet upstream benchmark can explicitly select off after its closed controller is checked. This does not establish a speed benefit; the stderr lines and CPU loop need separate attribution.
2. **Faster hash:** a different hash may reduce CPU time, but changing the algorithm changes the diagnostic identity and any existing cross-run comparison meaning. Benchmark the current FNV separately from candidate hashes over the actual byte sizes and CPU/runtime; document algorithm and seed in the field name/protocol. It still must not replace exact readback comparison. FNV's byte recurrence is serial (`h[i+1] = (h[i] ^ byte) * prime`), so a STREAM-like bandwidth result cannot be assumed to predict it; a bulk memory bandwidth benchmark is not a hash benchmark.
3. **Compute or reuse source hash elsewhere:** hashing while comparing can avoid a second source traversal only if exact equality remains unconditional and measurement demonstrates no regression versus optimized `memcmp`. A scalar fused compare/hash loop may be slower than the library `memcmp`. Precomputed immutable-source hashes can avoid repeated source scans only if the digest is already produced and validated at source ingestion, bound to an immutable source identity/lifetime, and available for every selected blob. It does not verify the destination and cannot be treated as a substitute for the checked readback comparison. No such per-blob digest contract was found in the inspected `phase_fill` call path.

Do not claim that the unaccounted R375 1,406.742 ms is FNV or logging. R375's subtraction is an accounting gap containing uninstrumented source lookup, logging/hash, loop/control and runtime/measurement effects; the share from each remains unknown. R375's bounded 48-group batching and readback-USM proposals are independent topics and are not repeated here.

## Minimum evidence needed to attribute cost

Use serialized, closed-run instrumentation that keeps all correctness gates on. Split per-fill host time into: source lookup; write submission plus checked completion; readback submission plus checked completion; exact compare; FNV byte walk; formatting/write of the slot line; and remaining loop/control. Record call count, total bytes, size distribution, per-stage wall time and whether stdout/stderr is redirected or terminal-backed. Do not sum nested counters as if independent wall time. To isolate logger cost, compare detailed versus hash-without-line versus neither, with the same exact comparisons and input order. To isolate hash cost, compare current FNV-on against off, and any candidate hash, over identical pre-touched immutable bytes with warm-up and repeated CPU-only trials; include compiler/build identity, CPU affinity/frequency policy, byte count and cache state. Report distributions and total time, not only throughput peak.

For an initial low-cost diagnostic, CPU-only runs over representative blob sizes can estimate hash and formatting costs, but they cannot establish GPU phase-refill wall-time benefit because they omit the interleaved checked GPU transfers and actual logging destination. A trace-stage counter around hash and logging on a future serialized real refill can directly measure their contributions; retain exact payload comparison and checked SYCL completion in every treatment. A quiet upstream `bench.sh` OFF/ON comparison remains the performance decision evidence; a source-only audit or CPU microbenchmark is not speed qualification.

## Primary references and interpretation

- Khronos [SYCL 2020 specification, USM allocation characteristics and explicit memcpy requirements](https://registry.khronos.org/SYCL/specs/sycl-2020/html/sycl-2020.html): host USM is host-resident and accessible to host/devices under context rules; SYCL memcpy accepts host or device-accessible USM pointers. These are memory-access and API-contract statements, not a throughput guarantee.
- Level Zero [zeMemAllocHost](https://oneapi-src.github.io/level-zero-spec/level-zero/latest/core/api/apis/mem.html#zememallochost): host memory is host-owned, accessible to host and devices in the context, and frequently used as a staging area. This supports considering the allocation class, but says nothing quantitative about this application's pageable vector readback, nor does it change the mandatory checked readback/equality contract.
- Intel [DPC++ Compatibility Tool release notes](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/release-notes/dpcpp-compatibility-tool/2021.html): notes that `queue.memcpy` may not provide expected performance on a DPC++ CPU device. This is a narrowly scoped vendor note showing that API choice alone does not imply performance; it is not evidence for GPU FNV cost or a result for Strata's Level Zero device.

No authoritative source located in this audit provides an applicable measured cost for this byte-wise FNV walk or stderr formatting. External references do not establish an expected speedup or qualify any candidate.

## Prior evidence and status

The closed v2 lifetime summary reports 768 successful payload writes, readbacks and compares; `H2D=1,571,635,200 B / 1,441.241 ms`, `D2H=1,571,635,200 B / 412.846 ms`, `memcmp=78.016 ms`, and `grow_fill_publish=3,364.974 ms`. These diagnostic-run counters identify the measured components only. R375 records the 1,406.742 ms subtraction as an unmeasured residual and names FNV/logging as possible contributors, not an attribution. The summary labels that lifetime diagnostic ineligible for performance and quality qualification. No source behavior, build, test, benchmark result, or speed-fit/quality claim is added by R377.

This report is supplemental to R375, not a correction to its conclusions. Registry v188 supplies the report count 917; no registry mutation or report registration was performed in this read-only supplemental audit.
